prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, the make/age of your system, whether it’s an emergency, and whether you want lowest price vs. a longer warranty or a maintenance plan. I can give a short list of top-rated Phoenix companies if you tell me your ZIP and whether you need same‑day service. Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical guide to get you started.

Quick troubleshooting (safe, immediate things to try)
- Check the thermostat: is it set to COOL and below room temp? Replace the batteries.
- Check the air filter: if clogged, replace it.
- Check the breaker panel: reset any tripped breakers for the AC circuit.
- Check the outdoor unit: clear debris, make sure the switch on the disconnect box near the unit is on.
If none of the above help or the unit is making unusual noises or the compressor isn’t running, call a pro.

How to pick the best HVAC company in Phoenix
- Licensing: Verify the contractor is licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (AZ ROC).
- Certifications: Ask for NATE-certified technicians and EPA Section 608 certification (for refrigerant work).
- Insurance: Confirm they carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Reviews & complaints: Check Google Reviews, Yelp, and the BBB for recent ratings and how the company handles complaints.
- Written estimate & scope: Get a written estimate that lists parts, labor, diagnostics fee, and warranty.
- Warranties: Ask about manufacturer and contractor warranties for parts and labor.
- Experience with your system: Confirm they’ve worked on your brand/model and can get replacement parts.
- Upfront pricing: Beware of very low “bait” prices — get at least 2–3 quotes for comparable scopes.
- Maintenance plans: If you plan to stay in your home, a company offering annual tune‑ups with priority service can be worth it.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed in Arizona? What’s your ROC number?
- Are your techs NATE and EPA certified?
- Do you charge a diagnostic fee and is it applied toward repairs?
- What’s your response time for emergency service?
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?
- Can you provide recent references or local reviews?

If you give your ZIP code (and say whether it’s an emergency), I’ll list several well-reviewed Phoenix HVAC companies near you and what to expect from each.
